RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the March 19, 2007/Phalguna 28, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Earth Sciences; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource
Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable
Energy; Power; Science and Technology; Social Justice and Empowerment;
Tribal Affairs; Women and Child Development)
Total number of questions — 20
89
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Implementation of RGGVY in Bihar
and Maharashtra
*281. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) the number of villages electrified
under the Rajiv Gandhi Grameen
Vidyutikaran Yojana during the last two
years in Bihar and Maharashtra, district-
wise;
(b) whether it is a fact that the
implementation of this scheme is not
satisfactory in these States;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps Government are taking for
100 per cent implementation of this
scheme?
Power projects for Commonwealth
Games
*282. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have ear-
marked five power projects with a
generating capacity of 4,980 mw for Delhi
which will be ready by 2010
Commonwealth Games;
(b) the names of these five power
projects;
(c) the status of their implementation;
(d) whether Government are reducing
priority for other power projects,
earmarked to meet energy shortages in States
like Andhra Pradesh; and
(e) the steps proposed by Government
to ensure even-handed and equal
development of the power sector all over
the country?
Participation    of    food    processing
industry in the international market
†*283. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
participation of Indian food processing
industry in the international market is very
unsatisfactory;

90
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto;
(c) whether its exports can be increased
by giving momentum to research and
investigation in this industry; and
(d) if so, the reaction of Government in
this regard and what is the action plan in
this direction?
Gas purchased by NTPC
†*284. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that gas is
purchased under the National Thermal
Power Corporation for the gas based power
projects;
(b) if so, the estimated requirement of
gas during the year 2006-07;
(c) the means through which this
requirement has been met;
(d) the prices paid separately for the
same; and
(e) the reasons for different prices
having been paid, instead of a uniform price,
for purchasing gas?
Mid-day Meal in schools
*285. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are ensuring
that the children are getting meal daily as
per entitlement in the Mid-day Meal
Scheme in schools for children from primary
to secondary;
(b) if so, the steps taken or proposed to
be taken in this regard;
(c) whether it is possible to provide
better quality meal within the same
resources;
(d) if so, whether Government called
for any meeting with States to discuss this
issue;
(e) if so, the issues discussed in the
meeting; and
(f) the outcome thereof?
Improvement in the primary
education system
*286. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the steps taken to improve the
primary education system in the country;
and
(b) whether Government are going to
increase the strength of teachers from First
class to Eighth class, which is the base of
the education?
15 point programme for minorities
*287. SHRI PENUMALLI MADHU:
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that
recommendations of the 15 point
programme for Muslim minorities, which
made it mandatory for selection
committees to have representation
from the minorities have not been followed;
and
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government
in this regard?

91
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Trade unions among Anganwadi
Workers
†*288. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the Minister of WOMEN
AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether her Ministry is aware of
the fact that any workers' union or trade
union is functional among Anganwadi
Workers;
(b) if so, the number of such unions
throughout the country alongwith the
names of major trade unions among such
unions; and
(c) whether any delegation of these
unions has ever held a meeting with the
Minister and submitted any memorandum
to Government?
Demands of Anganwadi Workers
*289. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether a review committee has been
set up as desired by the Prime Minister to
look into the demands of Anganwadi
Workers and Helpers;
(b) whether there is any specific demand
by them, and if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have decided
to meet their demands;
(d) if so, the number of Anganwadi
Workers and Helpers expected to be
benefited in the country;
(e) whether any financial assistance has
been accorded therefor; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
Illegal mining in Rajasthan
†*290. SHRI BANWARI LAL
KANCHHAL: Will the Minister of
MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether saints and public are
expressing their severe anger in protest
against illegal mining taking place in the
holy mountains situated at Brij Chaurasi
Kos in Deeng and Kama tehsil of District
Bharatpur, Rajasthan;
(b) whether the Supreme Court,
Rajasthan High Court and the Department
of Archaeology have declared the mining
illegal;
(c) whether Government will conduct
an enquiry regarding the ongoing illegal
mining despite the ban thereon and the
matter being in the knowledge of the
Minister of Mines of Rajasthan
Government;
(d) whether the illegal mining will be
stopped keeping in view religious and
environmental issues; and
(e) if so, by when and if not, the reasons
therefor?
Right to Education Bill
*291. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry's most
ambitious project the Right to Education
Bill has run into serious trouble as the State
Governments do not feel confident about
Minister's assurance that the Centre would
meet the major share of expenditure to be
incurred on its implementation;
(b) if so, the main objections raised by
the States in this regard;
(c) the States that have raised the
objections;

92
(d) the assurance given by the Ministry
to the States regarding its commitment; and
(e) by when, a final decision for
introducing the Right to Education Bill will
be taken?
Amendments in MMDR Act
†*292. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
make amendment in the schedule of Mines
and Minerals Development and Regulation
Act (MMDR Act), 1957 on the basis of
recommendations made by the Hoda
Committee;
(b) whether this will not encourage the
monopolistic tendencies; and
(c) whether this will not affect the
system of taking decision by the State
Governments on their own and their
autonomy?
Setting up of additional IISERs
*293. SHRI VIJAYKUMAR RUPANI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
propose to set up more Indian Institutes
of Science Education and Research (IISER)
in addition to Pune and Kolkata;
(b) the number of IISERs proposed to
be set up in the Eleventh Five Year Plan;
(c) by when these new IISERs will be
set up and commence their activities;
(d) whether Government plan to set up
an IISER in Gujarat soon;
(e) if so, the details in this regard; and
(f) the criteria for setting up an IISER in
the country?
Committee to review NCERT
textbooks
*294. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether, battling with the
controversy over NCERT textbooks, his
Ministry have decided to set up a
committee under former UGC Chairman
to go into the contents of these books;
(b) if so, the main aims/objectives of
this committee;
(c) by when this committee is likely to
submit its report; and
(d) if the report has been submitted, the
details thereof?
Lack of science laboratories in schools
†*295. SHRI BRIJ BHUSHAN
TIWARI:
SHRI JANESHWAR
MISHRA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that according to
the Seventh State Survey Report of
NCERT, 20 per cent of schools lack
laboratories for science subjects;
(b) if so, the State-wise details of such
schools;
(c) whether Government would
formulate any programme to improve
academic standard of such schools and
provide all required means/equipments; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

93
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Rural electrification in Madhya
Pradesh
†*296. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that under the
Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran
Yojana, the schemes of 47 districts of
Madhya Pradesh have been sent to the
Rural Electrification Corporation;
(b) if so, the number of schemes
sanctioned so far out of these and the amount
involved therein; and
(c) the status of the pending schemes,
the reasons therefor and by when these
schemes would be given approval?
Coverage of Mid-day Meal Scheme
†*297. SHRI SATYAVRAT
CHATURVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that as per the
official figures, during the years 2002 to
2005, Mid-day Meal was provided to
2,98,52,000 children in Rajasthan whereas
the actual number of children was not more
than 150 crore;
(b) when this fact had come to the
knowledge of Government;
(c) the persons found guilty in the said
case and the action taken against them; and
(d) the steps taken by Government to
prevent such incidents in the future?
Schemes for backward minorities and
weaker sections
†*298. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
real condition of educationally-backward
Muslims and minorities;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the efforts being made by
Government for implementation of
educational schemes for the benefit of
educationally-backward minorities,
especially of weaker sections;
(d) the success achieved in making
minorities literate under such schemes; and
(e) the financial assistance provided to
Non-Governmental Organisations in
Uttar Pradesh by the Maulana Azad
Shiksha Pratisthan during the last three
years?
Amendments in NCW Act
*299. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether any measures are being
contemplated by Government for
amendments to the National Commission
for Women Act;
(b) the measures taken by Government
to ensure functional autonomy for NCW;
and
(c) whether NCW enjoys a similar status
granted to other such commissions?

Literacy in the country
*300. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the percentage
of literate persons in Kerala is 100 per cent
in comparison to other States in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(c) the steps Government propose to
take in order to help other States also for
upgradation of facilities/to increase the
percentage of literate persons on the Kerala
model; and
(d) the details of budgetary allocations
made during 2007-08 in comparison to
2006-07?

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the March 19, 2007/Phalguna 28, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Earth Sciences; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource
Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable
Energy; Power; Science and Technology; Social Justice and Empowerment;
Tribal Affairs; Women and Child Development)
Total number of questions — 155
487
Study on Avalanches
†2107. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of
EARTH SCIENCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
conducted or propose to conduct any
study on national calamities like landslide
and avalanche hitting some parts of the
country almost every year;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether any system is in place to
identify such places for precautionary
measures; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Study on global warming
†2108. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of
EARTH SCIENCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether any scientific study on
impact of global warming on climatic
changes, has been conducted;
(b) whether various parts of the country
have witnessed such extreme conditions of
climate such as tsunami, excessive rains,
and drought because of this impact;
(c) if so, the details of areas most
affected by climatic changes; and
(d) the details of international
deliberations on this issue, various aspects
concerning its prevention, and consensus
arrived at various fora to overcome its
impact?
Impact of increasing temperature of
earth
†2109. SHRI DILIP SINGH JUDEV:
Will the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether increase in the temperature
of the earth is having its direct impact in
the country resulting in melting of the
glaciers and decline in the thickness of the
snow in the Himalayas;
(b) if so, the number of years since its
study is being done and the action being
taken to check this trend;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

488
(c) whether any direct effect has been
noticed so far as a result of the action taken;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Weather forecast by Meteorological
Department
†2110. SHRI MAHENDRA SAHNI:
Will the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that despite the
issuance of weather forecast by
Meteorological Department for the use of
farmers since 1977, it is still not reaching
the farmers in time;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the number of districts of the country
where facility of weather forecast is
accessible to the farmers at present
alongwith the number of districts which
are not getting the same facility?
Development of food processing
industries in Sikkim
2111. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have granted
any financial assistance to Sikkim for
development and promotion of food
processing industries;
(b) if so, the details thereof indicating
the total amount released to Sikkim for the
purpose during the last three years; and
(c) the details of new proposals
formulated by Government in this regard?
Food processing industries in the
country
†2112. SHRI BRIJ BHUSHAN
TIWARI:
SHRI JANESHWAR
MISHRA:
SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) total number of food processing
industries set up in the country, including
Uttar Pradesh, during the last three years;
(b) whether Government have
approved new projects for U.P. during the
current year;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the details of sanctioned and pending
projects during last three years, State-wise?
Food Processing Industries in Rajasthan
2113. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA:
SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) the total number of food processing
industries in Rajasthan;
(b) whether Government have
sanctioned any new projects in 2007-08;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) the number of project applications
received/sanctioned/rejected and pending
during the last three years; and
(e) the action Government propose to
take to prevent horticultural produce from
going waste, due to lack of processing
facilities in Rajasthan; and the probable
estimate of the waste?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

489
Food processing industries in
Jharkhand
†2114. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the number of food processing
industries in Jharkhand which have been
given approval during the last three years;
(b) the names of such food items which
are processed; and
(c) the efforts being made for revival of
sick units?
EDUSAT for training of teachers
2115. DR. K. KASTURIRANGAN:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether the country's educational
satellite, EDUSAT, is being used for the
training of teachers concerned with our
primary, secondary and higher secondary
education;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the plans for expanding the teachers'
training programme with EDUSAT in the
next two years; and
(d) the details of States in the country
which are not covered by this programme
and the plans of Government to bring them
also under this training programme in the
near future?
Corruption in Hindi Granth Academies
†2116. SHRI LAXMINARAYAN
SHARMA: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of cases of staff and
officers being involved in corruption in
Hindi Granth Academies established in
different States during the last two years;
(b) the action taken regarding
investigation in every academy and the
reasons for keeping the post vacant for
more than one year; and
(c) the steps that will be taken to
improve the condition and to fill up the
vacancies especially in Bihar Hindi Granth
Academy?
Addition of new IITs
2117. DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are planning
to add to the number of IITs that are already
present;
(b) whether it is a fact that Government
of Karnataka has requested the Central
Government to start an IIT in Karnataka;
(c) if so, Government have any plans to
start one in Karnataka; and
(d) what are the possible venues for
new IITs?
Attendance of Muslim children in
schools
2118. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether as per the report of Planning
Commission 12 per cent of Muslim children
in the age group of 6—13 years do not
attend school at all;
(b) if so, the details thereof,  State-wise;
and
(c) the steps being taken to encourage
them for school education?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

490
Expenditure of funds under SSA
2119. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 70 per cent
of funds allotted for Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
have already been spent by December,
2006;
(b) what is Government's reaction to
this fast rate of expenditure on S.S.A;
(c) whether Government have created a
perception where expenditure has been
viewed as the indication of the programm's
success; and
(d) the steps proposed to carefully
assess how the funds were spent and what
were the on-ground results?
Higher education in Andhra Pradesh
2120. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA : Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it has come to the notice of
his Ministry that in view of more than
expected enrolment of students under Sarva
Siksha Abhiyan, the enrolment of students
in higher classes, in Andhra Pradesh has
gone up and in the absence of necessary
infrastructure the State has taken
Rs. 303 crores from NABARD to improve
high school infrastructure;
(b) whether Government of Andhra
Pradesh requested his Ministry for
providing assistance to the tune of
Rs. 1,800 crores since Rs. 303 crores is not
adequate to meet the target; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and how his
Ministry are planning to support the State
in this respect?
Allocation for SSA and Mid-Day Meal
2121. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to reports published in print
media recently;
(b) if so, the amount Government are
going to allocate for Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
and Mid-day Meal Scheme during the
Eleventh Plan period as compared to Tenth
Plan period;
(c) whether it is a fact that his Ministry
has put forward the demand of Rs. 30,000
crore in this regard; and
(d) if so, the amount to be allocated by
Government?
Primary education in Andhra Pradesh
2122. SHRI C.
RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Andhra
Pradesh stands at one of the lowest place
in the primary education in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) what is the condition of other States
in the country; and
(d) the steps and long term plans
proposed to be made in this regard?
Appearing in other subjects in lieu of
maths
2123. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether CBSE has embarked on a
scheme to allow students to appear

491
compartmentally in other substitute
subjects if they fail in maths;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) to what extent this will affect the
level of maths in the country;
(d) what thought had been given by
CBSE before finalising this scheme; and
(e) the steps proposed by CBSE to
consider all consequences before embarking
on such schemes?
Visa for US scholars
2124. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that U.S. Scholars
from certain prestigious universities
applying to the Central Government to
research on various subjects of their choice
in Indian universities/institutes under the
Indo-US Fullbright Bilateral Scholarship
Exchange programme are denied visa or do
not get clearance from the concerned
authorities for months on end or asked to
change their topic of research, while the
Indian scholars visiting the U.S. under the
same programme get the necessary clearance
from the U.S. authorities immediately; and
(b) if so, the details with measures
proposed to be taken to correct the
situation?
Reduction of school fees to
compensate petro-price hike
2125. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
developing countries like Indonesia,
Malaysia and Ghana have sweetened the
politically bitter pill of petro-prices by
reducing or waiving school fees for children;
(b) if so, whether Government are
considering to follow suit; and
(c) if not, the reasons thereof?
Co-operation between India and
Pakistan in education
†2126. SHRI UDAY PRATAP
SINGH: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
upon formulating any scheme for the co-
operation in the field of education between
India and Pakistan; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Inadequacies in Government Schools
2127. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are cognizant
of inadequate quality of education,
educational infrastructure and other
necessary facilities in the neighbourhood
Government schools despite Government's
priority for providing quality education as
proclaimed in National Action Plan for
children;
(b) if so, whether Government have any
programme to improve the situation;
(c) if so, the details of such programme;
(d) whether Government have assessed
the impact of such programme of
Government run schools; and
(e) if so, the parameters thereof?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

492
National technological mission
2128. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA: W ill the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether in an attempt to avoid
criticism for deteriorating education
standards, his Ministry have proposed a
national technological mission for ushering
in technology driven education in
institutions of the country;
(b) if so, whether his Ministry have
submitted the scheme to the Planning
Commission for its approval; and
(c) if so, the details of the proposal and
by what time, his Ministry are likely to
implement the same?
Computer education in Kendriya
Vidyalayas and Navyug School
2129. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
impart computer education from fifth
standard onward in all Kendriya
Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalayas and
Navyug Schools;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Promotion of information technology
in schools
2130. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) the details of schemes and
programmes formulated and being
implemented by Government for
development and promotion of information
technology in Government schools of the
country;
(b) if so, the details of funds allocated
for computer training in rural areas of the
country particularly in Andhra Pradesh
during the last three year, State-wise;
(c) whether it is a fact that the funds
allotted for this purpose are not being
utilized by the concerned education
departments in the country; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and the
steps taken by Government in this regard?
Recommendation of C.N.R. Rao
